reference: Independent python implementation of the psychrometric mass and energy balances of all four paths (room moisture balance, wet cooling coil with the condensate/frost enthalpy, reheat, desiccant rotor with both sectors, heat-pump condenser/evaporator), using the ASHRAE Handbook-Fundamentals 2017 Ch.1 property set the tool declares, cross-checked point by point against CoolProp 8.0.0 HAPropsSI.
reference_citations: ASHRAE Handbook - Fundamentals (2017), Chapter 1 "Psychrometrics": Eq.(5) and (6) saturation pressure over ice and over liquid water, Eq.(20) humidity ratio, Eq.(30) specific enthalpy, Eq.(28) moist-air density, and the cooling/dehumidifying energy balance q = m_da[(h1 - h2) - (W1 - W2) h_w] with h_w the enthalpy of the condensate leaving the coil.
Hyland, R.W. and Wexler, A. (1983), ASHRAE Transactions 89(2A), 500-519 - the saturation pressure correlations behind Eq.(5)/(6).
CoolProp 8.0.0 HumidAirProp (ASHRAE RP-1485 real-gas moist air) - used as the second, structurally different property reference (see crosscheck).
tolerance: display-limited: half of the last digit the tool prints (specific energy 0.005 kWh/kg, duties 0.05 kW, water 0.005 kg/h, temperatures 0.05 K). The ASHRAE ideal-gas and CoolProp real-gas property sets differ by up to 0.5 % in humidity ratio and 0.007 K in dew point (see crosscheck), so a disagreement below that level is property scatter and is flagged rather than graded.

crosscheck.what: ASHRAE ideal-gas moist air (the formulation the tool implements) vs CoolProp 8.0.0 HAPropsSI (ASHRAE RP-1485 real gas)
crosscheck.note: CoolProp uses a different enthalpy datum for moist air, so the enthalpy difference below is a datum offset and not an error; the humidity ratio and dew point are datum-free and agree to the values shown. Duties are computed from enthalpy DIFFERENCES, so the datum cancels. Where the two property sets differ by more than the tolerance the tool is flagged, not graded.
